tagline: delighting consumers by lighting up everyday moments
hero_kpi_rationale: Critical operating margin reflecting pricing pressure and restructuring charges. Despite productivity efforts, margin collapses to 0.5% in 2025 (versus 0.9% in 2024), signaling a major operational deterioration requiring close monitoring.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total value of sales after discounts and returns.
kpis.description: Net sales declined in 2025 due to soft demand, particularly in the Home and Commercial Solutions and Outdoor and Recreation segments.
kpis.signal: 5% decline in 2025, impacted by weak demand and distribution losses.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin stands at 33.8% in 2025, slightly up from 33.6% in 2024, driven by productivity gains and pricing adjustments.

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.description: Operating margin drops to 0.5% in 2025 from 0.9% in 2024, heavily compressed by $114 million in tariff-related cost overruns, restructuring charges, and intangible asset impairments.

kpis.name: Net Loss
kpis.explanation: Total loss after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net loss amounts to $285 million in 2025, compared to $216 million in 2024, amplified by intangible impairments, tariff cost overruns, and restructuring activities.
kpis.signal: Net loss sharply higher at $285 million.

kpis.name: Restructuring Charges
kpis.explanation: Costs related to workforce reduction and restructuring plans.
kpis.description: Net restructuring charges amount to $62 million in 2025, including $40 million recorded in December under the Productivity Plan, primarily for severance payments. Total restructuring and restructuring-related charges: $90 million.
kpis.signal: $62 million in restructuring charges in 2025 (including $40 million in December for the Productivity Plan).

kpis.name: Tariff Cost
kpis.explanation: Additional cost borne by the company due to new tariffs.
kpis.description: The company incurred $174 million in incremental tariff costs in 2025 before mitigation, while only $114 million was recognized in cost of sales, creating a timing mismatch.
kpis.signal: $174 million in incremental tariff cost in cash in 2025.

kpis.name: Intangible Asset Impairment
kpis.explanation: Non-cash loss related to the write-down of brands deemed less valuable.
kpis.description: The company recorded a $340 million non-cash impairment on three brands (two in HCS, one in LD) due to downward revisions in projected cash flows and higher discount rates reflecting the decline in stock price.
kpis.signal: $340 million charge for impairment of three brands in Q4 2025.

kpis.name: Productivity Plan Charges
kpis.explanation: Total expected charges related to the productivity plan announced in December 2025.
kpis.description: The Productivity Plan, launched in December 2025, is expected to generate between $75 million and $90 million in charges, with $40 million already recognized in December 2025 and an additional $35 million to $50 million expected in 2026.
kpis.signal: Between $75 million and $90 million in charges expected by end of 2026.

kpis.name: Tariff Cost Timing Gap
kpis.explanation: Difference between tariff costs paid in cash and those recognized in operating results.
kpis.description: In 2025, the company paid $174 million in tariff-related cash outflows but recognized only $114 million in cost of sales, creating a $60 million timing gap to be recognized in future periods.
kpis.signal: $60 million timing gap between cash outflow and recognition in 2025.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 declared fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total Revenue of 14.742 Bn USD last fiscal year (FY2017).

ai_positioning.summary: Newell Brands is gradually integrating artificial intelligence tools into its commercial operations and consumer interactions, without positioning AI as a major strategic pillar. The focus is on process optimization and consumer understanding rather than disruptive innovation driven by AI.
evidence: mention of increasing adoption of digital tools and AI by consumers and retailers in the 10-K report
commercial strategy focused on consumer understanding, potentially supported by analytical and digital tools
absence of specific AI projects or dedicated AI KPIs in official documents
